ps140: 4, Podoben “As one valiant among the martyrs…”

Bound with chains, immured in prison,* given as food for wild beasts, hung aloft and mangled,* yet, receiving divine help from heaven, you remained unshaken* through the love of the Master and Saviour of all,* O most wise Carpus and Papylus.

Grounding your thought through wisdom on the rock of faith, O steadfast martyr Papylus,* you rejoiced when you were stoned,* likening yourself to the divine leader of martyrs, the archdeacon Stephen,* as a minister and servant of the mysteries of God,* as one numbered among the martyrs* and a converser with angels.

Unswervingly walking the path of witness, your feet nailed to iron sandals,* you steadfastly destroyed the sting of the enemy and destroyer, O all-praised ones,* and were crowned with victories.* Wherefore, all the Church of Christ celebrates* your holy, luminous, and renowned commemoration.

In that you were worthy among godly seers, O venerable one,* you beheld the heavens opened, and the Lord seated upon the throne,* and the cherubim and seraphim round about Him;* and we, your sacred flock, enlightened by you, O Carpus, cry out to you:* Ask for peace for the world and great mercy for our souls.
stavrotheotokion: Beholding our Life suspended upon the Tree,* O most immaculate Mistress, you cried out, lamenting maternally:* “O my Son and my God, save those who hymn You with love!”
